summary: Backdrop. US Treasury swap spreads track the supply/demand balance for Treasuries against a risk-free curve. Bank capital rules — the Supplementary Leverage Ratio, its enhanced version (eSLR), and the G-SIB surcharge — govern how much balance sheet dealers can commit to intermediating Treasuries; when the SLR binds, it caps demand for even riskless assets. [REDACTED] frames bank capacity through the lowest comfortable level of reserves (LCLOR): assuming QT ends with ~$2.9tn of reserves, an 11.5% LCLOR would allow bank assets to grow ~$1.2tn (5%), well inside the estimated $2.4-4.6tn SLR-reform capacity.
